data.title: DuPont, Illinois Tool Works cut to Neutral at J.P. Morgan on downside short-cycle trends
data.description:
DuPont and Illinois Tool Works were downgraded Friday to Neutral from Overweight with $145 and $277 price target, cut from $172 and $300, at J.P. Morgan, which cited concerns over decelerating short-cycle industrial demand into 2027.

"We are in a 'mid-cycle' stage of the industrial cycle - no longer 'early' - as many B2B/industrial end-market up-cycles are quite mature, and the AI up-cycle is entering year 4, [which] coupled with valuations which are not cheap vs. bond yields, caps the degree to which [electrical equipment and multi-industry sector] multiples can re-rate on a relative basis," JPM's Julian Mitchell said in a note.

The analyst said he has a "mildly positive" view of the EE/MI sector with scope for a "catch-up bounce" given the group's recent stock underperformance and likely positive estimate revisionmomentum at Q3 earnings.

JPM said its thesis on DuPont "primed for a short-cycle recovery with consistent execution" has largely played out, and while seeing improving trends for some pockets of the company's portfolio, "overall we see organic growth deceleration" into 2027 following above company average organic growth in 2026.

On Illinois Tool Works , Mitchell said he does "not view the overall short-cycle industrial complex particularly favorably, as we think manufacturing PMIs may not show much further improvement from current levels," meaning little opportunity for positive estimate revision at the company and a fair current valuation for the stock.

Additionally, JPM started Trane Trane at Overweight as "a best-in-class HVAC name, and we expect it to continue to thrive relative to the group and other HVAC pure-play names," and Carrier Global at Neutral as "valuation looks somewhat cheap, but there is considerable uncertainty over the earnings outlook."

data.title: US bonds slip as investors await inflation data, Fed signals
data.description:
Key points:
  • US 10-year yields may be nearing a peak, analyst says
  • US 2/10 yield curve flattens
  • US rate futures price in Fed interest rate pause this month

By Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss

US Treasuries fell on Friday, reversing some of the gains from earlier this week, as investors looked to upcoming inflation reports for clues on what the Federal Reserve will do at its October 27-28 policy meeting.

In afternoon trading, the benchmark 10-year yield was up 2.8 basis points (bps) at 5.261% after hitting a 24-year high earlier this week. On the week, however, 10-year yields were down 3.5 bps, the largest weekly drop in two months.

US 30-year yields were marginally higher at 5.608% (US30YT=RR), but fell 2.9 bps on a weekly basis. When Treasury prices fall, yields rise.

On the shorter end of the curve, US 2-year yields, which typically reflect interest rate expectations, climbed 4.4 bps to 4.799% (US2YT=RR). On the week, the yield declined 3.4 basis points.

"We saw just a little of a giveback after a pretty strong move this week in which we saw lower yields due to the strong 10-year and 30-year auctions," said Chip Hughey, managing director of fixed income at Truist Wealth in Richmond, Virginia.

"Yields across the curve really moved pretty sharply lower, so I think it's normal for the market to take a little breather after a move like we had this week," Hughey said.

Market participants looked ahead to inflation data next week, with the latest Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index reports due to be released on Wednesday and Thursday, respectively.

Ruchir Sharma, an economist at Nomura, wrote in a research note that core CPI inflation likely decelerated in September as the temporary boost to wireless telecom prices faded.

"Considering little urgency for consecutive rate hikes as well as the proximity to the midterm elections, our inflation forecast is unlikely to raise the likelihood of an October rate hike by the Fed," Sharma said.

US rate futures on Friday priced in an 80% chance the Fed will remain on hold at its policy meeting this month.

Treasury yields moved slightly higher after the University of Michigan showed that inflation expectations over the next year had increased in October to 4.7% from 4.6% in September. Twelve-month inflation expectations have surged from 3.4% in February before the US-Israeli war with Iran started.

The overall consumer sentiment index slumped further in early October to 46.3 from 48.1 last month.

Elsewhere in the Treasury market, the yield curve flattened for a second day on Friday, with the spread between 2-year and 10-year yields narrowing to 45.5 bps from 46.7 bps late on Thursday.

Friday's flattening largely reflected a reversal of steepening moves in the last few weeks as the market focused on inflation risks amid the rise in oil prices and concerns over the US fiscal outlook.

"We're nearing the higher end of where 10-year yields will go in the near term, barring a flare-up in the Middle East," Hughey said, noting that the market has seen buyers step in when the 10-year yield has approached the 5.30%-5.35% range.

"We have also seen that as the 10-year gets toward that range, the stock market has shown some discomfort and we have seen selloffs in risk assets and that has limited the 10-year's move higher," he added.

data.title: AST SpaceMobile Stock Is Down on SpaceX News-and It Shouldn't Be — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Al Root

SpaceX shook up the wireless communications industry on Thursday by buying more wireless spectrum, fueling disruption fears for traditional wireless companies.

Make no mistake, SpaceX wants to be a mobile wireless provider (as management has repeatedly said), but the traditional players will fight back as space- and land-based communications technology merge.

That should be good for shares of AST SpaceMobile, which aims to compete with SpaceX's space-based broadband product. AST stock is getting hammered on Friday, though. That's odd.

On Thursday, SpaceX announced the purchase of low-band spectrum for undisclosed terms. Low-band spectrum is good for broad wireless coverage and reaching inside buildings. It's another step on the path toward Starlink Mobile (or whatever Elon Musk decides to name SpaceX's mobile offering).

Shares of Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile were down between 10% and 13% in late Friday trading. Shares of wireless tower REITs American Tower and Crown Castle were up about 8% and 13%, respectively.

SpaceX's move is an endorsement of terrestrial wireless infrastructure, says Bernstein analyst Madison Rezaei. She describes the tower companies as apartment buildings. The tower apartments have three tenants — Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile — and might soon have a fourth.

Similarly, AST seems to be in a good position as wireless competition ramps up. Wireless carriers might be looking to the stars to fight SpaceX on its own turf. A satellite constellation operator that can move data around the globe would be a valuable ally. Still, AST shares were down almost 15% in midday trading on Friday.

That doesn't make sense to Berenberg analyst Michael Filatov. He sees AST as a natural choice for traditional companies looking to compete. Roth Capital also sees AST becoming the direct-to-device satellite partner for the traditional wireless industry.

Still, the stock is down. One reason could be that AST didn't buy the spectrum. It needs spectrum — the frequencies that carry data — to build its business. Still, the existing wireless players have a lot of spectrum, multiples of what SpaceX has accumulated.

MoffettNathanson analyst Craig Moffett said he was surprised by Friday's reaction, because everyone expected it. He also doesn't see SpaceX disrupting the three traditional carriers anytime soon. It still needs more infrastructure.

Elon Musk's company will still need to build more infrastructure, buy an existing player for their infrastructure, or partner with an existing player like Mint or Boost Mobile.

The spectrum buy might have been a gentle reminder to the traditional industry that partnering might be the least bad option.

Whatever happens, enablers of wireless communications are seeing their valuations increase. Investors should think about what that means for AST.

Write to Al Root at allen.root@barrons.com.

data.title: Wall Street posts weekly gains with earnings, inflation data on tap
data.description:
Key points:
  • Indexes up: Dow 0.83%, S&P 0.59%, Nasdaq 0.64%
  • SpaceX acquires low-band spectrum portfolio; telecoms drop
  • Apple falls on report of iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max component production cuts

By Stephen Culp and Tharuniyaa Lakshmi

Wall Street ended higher on Friday as investors shifted their focus to next week, with third-quarter earnings season set to start and inflation data expected, which could shed light on the Federal Reserve's next policy decision.

All three major US stock indexes advanced on the day, logging weekly gains. The small-cap Russell 2000 , however, ended lower than last Friday's close.

"It's the kind of back-and-forth market we've been in where we have the reversal of sentiment around Iran," said Ross Mayfield, investment strategy analyst at Baird in Louisville, Kentucky. "With conflicting headlines coming out of the White House and parties in the Middle East, there's just no edge there."

"That's why it's a fairly tepid rally," Mayfield added.

Crude prices initially retreated after President Donald Trump said the US will not launch any attacks on Iran before the midterm elections, adding that talks between Washington and Tehran aimed at ending the market-rattling Iran war were "productive."

Front-month West Texas Intermediate oil and Brent crude both settled up 0.4%.

Benchmark Treasury yields edged higher, but remained below Wednesday's 24-year high.

BANKS DUE TO REPORT EARNINGS

Third-quarter reporting season begins in earnest next week, with big US banks Wells Fargo , Goldman Sachs , Citigroup , JPMorgan Chase , Bank of America and Morgan Stanley scheduled to release results.

Analysts estimate S&P 500 annual earnings growth of 30.6%, on aggregate, for the July-September period, with energy and technology posting the largest year-on-year earnings growth of 123% and 66.5%, respectively, according to LSEG data.

The mood of American consumers, who shoulder about 70% of the US economy, has soured this month, according to the University of Michigan, with near-term expectations deteriorating to an all-time low.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 423.31 points, or 0.83%, to 51,654.95, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX gained 46.15 points, or 0.59%, to 7,811.51 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 172.83 points, or 0.64%, to 27,366.17.

Among the 11 major sectors of the S&P 500, communication services was the lone percentage loser.

AI-related momentum stocks were generally higher, with the Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF up 1% as the US bull market, largely driven by the AI boom, approaches its four-year anniversary.

"Chips have been this year's story," said Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager at Founder ETFs in Dallas. "(It's) a multidecade technological change and just at the beginning of whatever's happening, not at the end."

Elon Musk's SpaceX struck a deal to acquire a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio, posing a direct challenge to US wireless companies. Telecom firms T-Mobile US , AT&T , and Verizon dropped between 8.8% and 13.3%.

Humana jumped 11.6% after US government data showed 95% of the health insurer's members were in Medicare Advantage plans rated four stars or higher for 2027.

Apple slid 1.1% after a media report that the iPhone maker has told some suppliers to cut production of components for its newly launched iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, as soaring memory chip costs and price increases dampen consumer demand.

Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.65-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 141 new highs and 183 new lows on the NYSE.

On the Nasdaq, 2,756 stocks rose and 1,997 fell as advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.38-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 14 new 52-week highs and five new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 41 new highs and 209 new lows.

Volume on US exchanges was 14.37 billion shares, compared with the 17.76 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days.

data.title: Soybean, corn barge basis steady to mixed as harvest pace picks up
data.description:
Basis bids for soybeans and corn shipped by barge to the US Gulf were steady to mixed on Friday, as the harvest pace in the central US Midwest picked up and empty barges moved north to meet demand, traders said.

  • US corn futures plunged by as much as the daily trading limit on Friday on the Chicago Board of Trade, and ended sharply lower after the US Department of Agriculture shocked traders with an unexpected increase to its 2026 US harvest outlook.

  • CBOT wheat futures followed corn lower, pressured by the USDA's larger-than-expected stock forecast increase, while soybeans bounced from a six-week low to finish the day higher.

  • And spot basis bids for soybeans were generally flat to weaker in the US Midwest on Friday, pressured at a few soy processing sites by the accelerating harvest, dealers said.

  • The range between bids and offers for CIF soybean barges loaded in October widened sharply on Friday, traders said.

  • CIF soybean barges loaded in October were bid at 81 cents over CBOT November soybean (SX26) futures, down 5 cents, while November barge loadings were bid at 108 cents over futures, down 1 cent.

  • FOB export premiums for Gulf soybean shipments in October held steady at around 110 cents over CBOT November soybean (SX26) futures, while November shipments were offered at 117 cents over futures, up 2 cents.

  • CIF corn barges loaded in December traded at 97 cents over CBOT December corn (CZ26) futures.

  • Meanwhile, CIF corn barges loaded in October were bid at 72 cents over CBOT December corn (CZ26) futures, up 2 cents from Thursday, while corn barges loaded in November were bid at 87 cents over December futures, up 3 cents.

  • FOB export premiums for Gulf corn vessels loaded in the first-half of October were up 6 cents at 103 cents over CBOT December corn (CZ26) futures, while vessels loaded in last-half October were offered at 103 cents over December futures, up 8 cents.

data.title: Nasdaq CEO Flags Tens of Billions in New Wall Street Opportunity
data.description:
Nasdaq CEO Adena Friedman says tokenization could unlock tens of billions of dollars currently trapped in collateral, arguing blockchain technology could fundamentally change how money and securities move through global financial markets.

If you tokenize all those instruments along with the flow of money, then the collateral becomes very fluid, Friedman said at TOKEN2049 in Singapore.

Her argument goes beyond crypto speculation. Banks and other financial institutions routinely pledge Treasuries, equities, money-market instruments and other assets as collateral. Converting those assets, alongside cash, into transferable digital tokens could potentially make collateral easier to move and reuse, freeing capital that otherwise sits idle.

If we can tokenize money, then we can tokenize the flow of capital, Friedman said.

Nasdaq itself is already moving in that direction. The Securities and Exchange Commission approved Nasdaq's proposal in March allowing securities to trade in tokenized form, while the exchange is also developing an equity-token framework designed to preserve shareholder rights and existing market protections.

The regulatory backdrop has moved further recently. In September, the SEC granted temporary conditional relief allowing certain venues to trade tokenized U.S. stocks through permissioned on-chain systems, another indication that tokenized securities are moving closer to mainstream financial infrastructure.

Friedman also sees tokenization intersecting with another structural shift: 24/7 markets. Retail investors have pushed toward continuous trading for years, while institutions are now increasingly exploring ways to keep capital moving outside traditional market hours.

Investor Takeaway

The investment story here is much larger than simply putting stocks on a blockchain.

Tokenization could reshape settlement, collateral management, trading and asset servicing, potentially benefiting companies already positioned between traditional finance and digital assets.

Nasdaq has made that strategy increasingly tangible, including a recently announced $100 million investment in Kraken parent Payward as the companies work together on tokenized equities and always-on market infrastructure.

That puts Nasdaq alongside Coinbase , Robinhood , BlackRock , JPMorgan Chase and other financial players pursuing different parts of the tokenization opportunity.

The key question for investors is no longer whether Wall Street experiments with tokenization. It is whether those experiments become sufficiently liquid, regulated and scalable to move meaningful portions of the existing financial system on-chain.

data.title: Kidoz Inc. to Present at Planet MicroCap Showcase: TORONTO 2026 in Partnership with MicroCapClub on Wednesday, October 28, 2026
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / October 9, 2026 / Kidoz Inc. (the "Company"), announced that it will be presenting at the Planet MicroCap Showcase: TORONTO 2026 in partnership with MicroCapClub on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, at 10am (EST) at the Arcadian Loft in Downtown Toronto. Jason Williams, Chief Executive Officer of Kidoz Inc., will be hosting the presentation and answering questions at the conclusion.

Kidoz Inc. is a global AdTech software company that powers privacy-first, high-performance mobile advertising across children, teens, families, and general audiences. Through its Kidoz Safe Ad Network and Prado division, the Company delivers compliant, contextual campaigns at scale, enabling trusted engagement for brands while maintaining the highest standards of digital safety and privacy.

To access the live presentation, please use the following information:

Planet MicroCap Showcase: TORONTO 2026 in partnership with MicroCapClub

Date: Wednesday, October 28, 2026, at 10am (EST)

Webcast: https://www.meetmax.com/sched/event_136811/conference_home.html

Kidoz management will also be available for 1x1 meetings over the course of the entire event held between 27 - 29 October, 2026. To attend the conference and book a specific 1x1 investor meeting please make sure you are registered at https://www.meetmax.com/sched/event_136811/conference_home.html.

"We're excited to participate in the Planet MicroCap Showcase to share Kidoz's compelling investment story," said Jason Williams, CEO of Kidoz Inc. "The past year marked a pivotal inflection point for our company after significant technical investments were made to establish a market-leading position in the rapidly growing mobile gaming advertising ecosystem. Our unique combination of comprehensive SDK technology, Kite IQ AI capabilities, and complete advertising infrastructure positions us advantageously in this evolving landscape."

In our presentation Jason Williams will discuss the company's three core technology pillars that create sustainable competitive advantages and its expansion strategy beyond the market-leading kids focus to capture the broader mobile gaming audience of teens and adults.

The Planet MicroCap Showcase event runs from October 27 to 29, 2026, and offers a unique opportunity for investors to engage directly with innovative microcap companies through presentations and one-on-one meetings. Registration is expected to close soon, and one-on-one meeting scheduling will open shortly. Interested investors are encouraged to register promptly to secure participation.

For full details of the Company's operations and financial results, please refer to the Securities and Exchange Commission website at www.sec.gov or the Kidoz Inc. corporate website at https://investor.kidoz.net or on the https://www.sedarplus.com website.

About Planet MicroCap

Planet Microcap hosts the highest quality microcap in-person events in North America. The mission is to bring the best microcap investors, companies, and allocators together to gather, connect, and grow. For more information about Planet MicroCap, please visit: https://planetmicrocap.com/

About MicroCapClub

MicroCapClub is an exclusive forum for experienced microcap investors to share and discuss microcap companies (sub $1 billion market cap) trading on global markets. Since 2011, our members have profiled 1500+ microcap companies, 300+ have turned into multi-baggers. Investors can join our community by applying to become a member or subscribing to gain instant access. For more information, visit https://microcapclub.com/

About Kidoz Inc.

Kidoz Inc. (www.kidoz.net) is a full-stack global advertising platform powered by contextual AI, enabling brand performance in mobile games without personal data.

Originally developed for children's digital environments, where compliance and safety requirements are among the highest, Kidoz delivers privacy-first advertising without reliance on personal data tracking or behavioural profiling. Its technology combines proprietary SDK integrations, the Kidoz Privacy Shield, and the Kite IQ contextual AI engine to match advertising to content, environment, and geography, in alignment with COPPA, GDPR-K, Apple ATT, and global standards.

The platform supports both children's and all-ages audiences through its Kidoz and Prado offerings, enabling brands to scale performance across the global mobile gaming ecosystem using safe, trusted, contextual, privacy-first targeting.

Google-certified and Apple-approved, Kidoz reaches a global audience across mobile apps and games and is trusted by leading global brands.

Duff & Phelps Utility and Infrastructure Fund Inc. is a closed-end investment management company whose investment objective is to seek total return, resulting primarily from (i) a high level of current income, with an emphasis on providing tax-advantaged dividend income and (ii) growth in current income, and secondarily from capital appreciation. The utility industry is defined to include the following sectors: electric, gas, water, telecommunications, and midstream energy. The infrastructure industry is defined as companies owning or operating essential transportation assets, such as toll roads, bridges, tunnels, airports, seaports, and railroads. The firm seeks to provide specialty investment strategies that enhance client outcomes through active portfolio management and customized solutions, utilizing a process with values that include quality, reliability, and specialization. Investment strategies include U.S. and global real estate securities, global listed infrastructure, energy infrastructure, water, and clean energy. For more information visit dpimc.com.

data.title: Alpine Income Property Trust Announces Agreement to Acquire 13-Property Industrial Portfolio for $117.3 Million
data.description:
WINTER PARK, Fla., Oct. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Alpine Income Property Trust, Inc. (the "Company"), an owner and operator of single-tenant net leased commercial income properties, today announced that it has entered into an agreement to acquire a 13-property industrial portfolio for $117.3 million, or $63 per square foot.

The portfolio totals approximately 1.9 million square feet on approximately 209 acres across 11 states. The properties are 100% leased to nine tenants under absolute triple-net leases with a weighted average remaining lease term of 10.2 years, and no lease expires before late 2031. The tenants have operated at their respective sites for an average of approximately 40 years, and many have made significant investments in their facilities. Approximately 19% of in-place cash rent is attributable to tenants that are rated investment grade or are subsidiaries of investment grade rated parents.

"This acquisition will add a portfolio of mission-critical manufacturing and distribution facilities, at a low basis with 10 years of weighted average lease term remaining," said John P. Albright, President and Chief Executive Officer of Alpine Income Property Trust. "We believe that the investment will deliver an attractive initial yield, and that the annual rent escalators built into the leases will support future cash flow growth."

The acquisition is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions. The Company expects to fund the acquisition with borrowings under its revolving credit facility, proceeds from select dispositions, and commercial loan repayments.

About Alpine Income Property Trust, Inc.

Alpine Income Property Trust, Inc. is a publicly traded real estate investment trust that seeks to deliver attractive risk-adjusted returns and dependable cash dividends by investing in, owning and operating a portfolio of single tenant net leased commercial income properties that are predominately leased to high-quality publicly traded and credit-rated tenants. The Company also complements its income property portfolio by strategically investing in a select portfolio of commercial loan investments intended to deliver an attractive risk-adjusted return.

We encourage you to review our most recent investor presentation which is available on our website at http://www.alpinereit.com.

data.title: Accendra Health, Inc. (ACH) Gets NYSE $1 Price-Compliance Notice
data.description:
Accendra Health received an NYSE notice that its average closing price was below $1 over 30 days. It has six months to cure and may consider a reverse stock split; shares remain listed during the cure period.

Material Details

#DetailAI Analyst View
1NYSE $1.00 price deficiency noticeFlags listing risk; often pressures shares and liquidity.
230-day avg price below $1.00Confirms sustained weakness, not a single-day dip.
3Six-month cure period grantedSets a compliance deadline that can drive headlines.
4Reverse split under considerationCan mechanically lift price but may signal distress.
5Stock remains on NYSE for nowNo immediate delisting; trading continuity preserved.

Context by AI Analyst

This is a late-stage confirmation of sustained share price weakness triggering NYSE compliance action. A concrete cure plan, price recovery above $1 for 30 days, or shareholder approval of a reverse split would turn this into a larger catalyst.
